title: Tanzanian Poured Bread
community: Zanzibar and coastal Tanzania — a unique ancient bread
author: Chef Fatuma

heritage.origin: Zanzibar — one of the most ancient Swahili coastal bread traditions
heritage.history: Mkate wa Kumimina (literally "poured bread") is made from a fermented rice flour batter that is poured into a greased tin and steamed or baked. It is one of the most ancient Swahili coastal breads — predating the arrival of wheat on the coast. Made from rice flour and coconut milk, it is naturally gluten-free and was the original bread of the coast before wheat flour became widely available.
traditionalUtensils: Large round baking tin or clay dish
heritage.modernEvolution: Now baked in the oven or steamed — both methods are used. The overnight fermentation remains non-negotiable for authentic flavour and texture.

desc: Mkate wa Kumimina — Zanzibar's ancient poured bread. A fermented rice flour and coconut milk batter poured into a tin and baked until set — gluten-free, naturally sweet, and fragrant with cardamom. One of the oldest breads of the Swahili coast.
longDesc: Mkate wa Kumimina is one of the most historically significant foods of the Tanzanian coast — made from rice flour and coconut milk rather than wheat, it predates the arrival of flour-based breads. The overnight fermentation, the pouring technique, and the result — a slightly dense, fragrant, naturally gluten-free bread — are entirely distinctive.
equipment: Round baking tin or loaf tin
steps: Dissolve yeast and sugar in warm water. Rest 10 minutes.
Whisk rice flour, cardamom, and salt in a bowl.
Add coconut milk, yeast mixture, and eggs. Whisk until completely smooth.
Cover and ferment overnight (8 hours minimum).
Bake at 180°C for 25—30 minutes until set and golden on top, or steam covered for 25 minutes.
chefTips: Overnight fermentation is essential — the slight tanginess and rise come from it.
The batter should be pourable — thinner than cake batter.
Greasing the tin generously prevents sticking.
cookingScience: See TZA005 (Vitumbua) for rice flour fermentation science. In mkate wa kumimina, the tin contains the foam structure produced by fermentation, resulting in a bread-like structure despite the absence of gluten.
sustainabilityTips: Entirely from coastal Tanzanian ingredients — rice, coconut, eggs.
culturalNote: Mkate wa Kumimina is a living piece of Zanzibar's pre-wheat food history — one of the few ancient coastal breads that survives in daily use. It represents the ingenuity of Swahili coastal communities in creating bread from what the land and sea provided long before wheat flour arrived.
